Autocraft began as a Mac live wallpaper in Swift and SceneKit: the AIs played on your desktop background.

Now it's an Unreal Engine 5 game. The simulation came over as engine-free C++20, and the Swift version retired on 5 October.

The longer you drive a kind of unit, the better every unit of that kind gets, but only while you drive it. Units the AI runs never level.

Each level offers two upgrades, you keep one. 216 across twelve unit kinds, and a reason to drive the Prospector.

Click any of your units and the camera dives in, 1.2 s from the top-down view to first person.

WASD walks, mouse aims, click fires, R uses its ability, V switches to third person. Esc hands it back to the AI commander.

Every game run an agent starts is hidden and silent: a Dock-less copy of the editor, rendering offscreen, sound rendered to a WAV file.

So an agent can test and record the game while I keep working on the same M4 Max MacBook Pro.

The whole simulation of my RTS (economy, pathing, combat, the AI commanders) is plain C++20 with no Unreal in it.

Unreal only draws the frames, plays the sounds and takes the input.

The core's tests build with plain clang and run in about 7 seconds:

make -C unreal/core-tests

That split is what lets AI agents change the game safely. They run the 7-second tests, not the editor.

The Longbow is a tank that anchors into artillery. Like every unit in Autocraft, you can drive it.

Down the ramp, anchor, shell the base, walk it on its siege legs, pack up, fire on the move. Top-down, first and third person, day into night.

My agents test and record Autocraft on the same M4 Max MacBook Pro I'm working on, and I don't notice.

Every game run they start is hidden and silent: a Dock-less copy of the editor, rendering offscreen. Sound goes to a WAV file. Nothing reaches my speakers.

Screenshot: one of them recording a clip while I keep working.

The music plays as a radio station: KSTR 88.7 Stardust, original songs with in-world ads between them.

Quicksilver Cola is pumped from Metallic Hydrogen wells and is not a beverage. Opal Glow face scrub side effects include levitation and being mined.

A 10 s clip of Autocraft used to take about 7 minutes to record. Now it takes 25 s.

Before, every frame was saved as a PNG, then encoded. Now frames are read back from the GPU asynchronously and piped raw into ffmpeg while the game runs.

In Autocraft you don't micromanage. Your team's AI commander runs the army.

Press M for the command map. Set a stance, pick objectives (attack, defend, hold, man a Bastion), call expansions, make requests. The AI plans the rest.

Click a building and press its buttons. If the AI can do it for you, the order goes to your commander's queue.

Each pane is a Claude Code agent working on its own part of Autocraft, all in the same repo at the same time.

When their work overlaps, they combine it with a three-way merge, never by copying whole files over each other.
